title: Freeze the demo as v1
request: Keep the redesigned demo as demo v1, the agreed reference for development: the product must look and behave exactly like it, and nobody edits the demo from now on.
spec: The tag demo-v1 and a note in the demo's README that it is the frozen reference. Done when git tag -l demo-v1 prints it, docs/product-demo/README.md says 'Demo v1', and python docs/product-demo/build.py --check passes.
plan: Add a 'Demo v1: frozen reference for development' note to docs/product-demo/README.md.
Tag the demo commit as demo-v1 with an annotated message.
Keep the demo's build --check inside make rd-check so it stays buildable.
Ask the owner before pushing main, dev and the tag; push once approved.

decisions.decision: The product frontend is a copy of the demo, never the demo itself.
decisions.why: The frozen demo is the yardstick; editing it would remove the reference the product is compared against.

decisions.decision: Pushing waited for the owner's explicit yes.
decisions.why: A push changes the shared repository; the package prompt asks for approval first.

change: Annotated tag demo-v1 on the demo commit ('Demo v1: the agreed UI and UX, frozen reference for building the product') and the frozen-reference note in the demo README.
outcome: Done: tag demo-v1 exists and was pushed with main and dev after the owner approved. Later fixes (phone-width top bar, fonts) went into the product only; demo v1 keeps its own copy.
lessons: Freeze the agreed design with a tag before building on it, so every later page can be compared against something that does not move.
